exercises.title: One letter, not two
exercises.body: The r-vowels are the trap of Shavian writing. English spells car with an a and an r, so the hand wants to write 𐑭𐑮 — but it is a single letter: 𐑒𐑸, two letters in all. Never write 𐑮 after a vowel; reach for the r-vowel instead.

exercises.title: Air, err, and ear
exercises.body: Three more sit on the same rows: 𐑺 for the air of hair, 𐑻 for the err of bird, 𐑽 for the ear of near. Say each word and listen for where your tongue goes — the vowel and the r arrive together, as one sound.

exercises.title: A whole word in one letter
exercises.body: Some r-vowels are words on their own: ear is just 𐑽, are is just 𐑸. And the tired -er that ends so many English words is 𐑼 — letter is 𐑤𐑧𐑑𐑼, sister 𐑕𐑦𐑕𐑑𐑼.
